stories.title: Utilities in Rawalpindi barred from digging up roads without permission
summary: Commissioner Rawalpindi Salman Ghani issued the directive at a meeting held to review road-cutting permissions and the installation and management of underground utility lines by various government departments.
He said all concerned departments must ensure comprehensive planning and effective coordination before undertaking any road-cutting activity.
All restoration work, including refilling and reconstruction, must be completed within 15 days of road cutting, he said.

stories.title: Proposed amendments to Islamabad LG law cast doubt on Dec 20 polls
summary: The report on the Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government (Amendment) Bill, 2026 (Ordinance No. II of 2026), was presented by committee chairman Raja Khurram Shahzad Nawaz of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) during Thursday’s session of the National Assembly.
The government introduced the bill in March this year, but the committee’s report was presented a day after the ECP announced the election schedule.

The federal government continued to postpone elections, citing various reasons, including proposed amendments to the Local Government Act, depriving around 2.5 million Islamabad residents of an elected local government system.

stories.title: ATC indicts PAF officer’s murderer, summons witnesses
summary: ISLAMABAD: An Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) on Thursday indicted an accused arrested in connection with the murder of Group Captain Asim Tariq, and summoned prosecution witnesses to record their statements.
Judge Abual Hasnat Mohammad Zulqarnain of the ATC conducted the hearing, during which the accused, Saad Abbasi, was produced before the court.
Police have registered a case against the accused at Margalla Police Station in connection with the murder.

stories.title: Growers critcise PTB for failing to purchase surplus tobacco
summary: The sources said PTB’s role in handling tobacco affairs is critical, but its officials always toe the line of companies, leaving the poor growers high and dry.
However, they said the companies were adopting delaying tactics or were not at all interested in buying the surplus tobacco from growers.
Iqbal Khan Shewa, the association’s patron-in-chief, told Dawn that both companies and traders exploited the weak financial position of tobacco growers.

stories.title: Illegal shops, business centres razed in Charsadda, Lakki Marwat
summary: Also, an anti-encroachment operation has been launched in Tangi tehsil under the supervision of assistant commissioner Akhlaq Ahmad and additional assistant commissioner Adan Zahid to reclaim land.
Traders complained about the operation in Sherpao Bazaar, claiming that their shops were demolished without prior notice, causing them serious financial issues.

Deputy commissioner Shahid Rafiq Gandapur led the operation wherein anti-encroachment squad of the tehsil municipal administration removed illegal buildings and structures from both sides of the busy Peshawar-Karachi Highway in the Serai Gambila Bazaar.

stories.title: Delayed filing of ownership statements: Lahore High Court annuls SECP penalties on mill directors
summary: The SECP had fined each director Rs60,000 under the Securities Act, 2015, for a 253-day delay in filing Form 5 after their re-appointment.
The judge also noted that an SECP clarification of April 20, 2022, indicated ambiguity over whether Form 5 applied to re-appointment of the same directors.
The judge allowed the appeals and set aside the orders of the SECP and its appellate bench.

stories.title: Seven suspects gunned down in Karachi ‘encounters’
summary: According to officials at the Taimuria police station, a team of the Shaheen Force signaled two riders of a motorcycle to stop for checking near the DC Office in North Nazimabad, but they opened fire and tried to speed away.
They were chased along the road running parallel to the DC office, the police said, adding that in the ensuing encounter, both the suspects were shot dead.
The Korangi police also claimed to have shot dead two suspected criminals in an ‘encounter’.

stories.title: Couple shot dead in coach near Sukkur; two held
summary: SUKKUR: A couple who had contracted a free-will marriage were shot dead in a passenger coach on the National Highway near the VIG Gate, within the limits of the Baiji Sharif police station in Panu Aqil, Sukkur district, on Thursday evening.
Acting on information, Baiji Sharif police reached the spot and arrested two suspects, Abdul Malik Samejo and Abdul Hanan Samejo, along with a repeater shotgun.
A free-will affidavit dated Sept 28, 2026, identifies a woman named Sidra, daughter of Abdul Hakeem Samejo, and gives details of her previous marriage to a man named Abdul Hanan.

stories.title: Faisalabad rickshaw drivers protest against LPG overcharging
summary: TOBA TEK SINGH: Scores of rickshaw drivers staged a protest demonstration at the District Council Chowk in Faisalabad on Thursday against alleged overcharging and black-marketing of LPG cylinders.
ACCIDENT: A minor child died after a speeding car ran him over near the Millat Road Chowk in Faisalabad.
The child, identified as Arbaz, was critically injured and shifted to the Allied Hospital where he died.

stories.title: In-custody suspect killed in ‘encounter’ in Lahore
summary: A police official claimed that the CCD team was taking the suspect, identified as Noor, for the recovery of looted items when his armed accomplices opened fire on the police.
Resultantly, the suspect was allegedly killed by the firing of his own accomplices, the police official claimed.
The police official claimed that the suspect was involved in several criminal activities.

stories.title: Tensions with Karachi Metropolitan Corporation flare as railways calls in armed personnel from other cities
summary: The KMC alleged PR policemen assaulted the City Wardens director before taking him to the railways police station.

Although the City Wardens director was released after hours of talks between the two sides, the KMC high-ups moved the Sharea Faisal police to lodge an FIR against the PR police officials for kidnapping and assaulting their officer.

In separate letters to senior Pakistan Railways police officials in the two cities, the department has asked them to release a certain number of personnel “along with arms and ammunition” for deployment in Karachi.

stories.title: Vehari police book alleged rapists of woman, recover her three kidnapped kids
summary: BAHAWALPUR: The Miranpur police in Vehari district claimed on Thursday to have recovered three abducted children from the illegal custody of three suspects, who had also been booked for the alleged gang-rape of the victims’ mother in the Kukri Kalan area of Mauza Gurdawar.
Miranpur SHO Saeedur Rehman said the police recovered the abducted children and raids were underway to arrest the suspects.

This was stated by Bahawalpur Commissioner Irfan Ali Kathia, while chairing a high-level meeting to review operational arrangements, the construction of new bus stands, and related infrastructure across all tehsil headquarters in the division.

stories.title: Residents write to CM Murad, urge halt to construction on Karachi's Nehr-i-Khayyam
summary: Clifton Neighbourhood Association seeks disclosure of project documents, an independent drainage study and EIA; demands restoration of waterway to its original width At the meeting, the residents again raised their objections and sought answers from the project representatives.

They called for the complete project report, approved engineering drawings, details of the engineering firm and responsible engineers, and the PC-I, including the project scope, cost and approvals, to be made publicly available.

Residents stressed that a project involving proposed changes to a major urban waterway must be supported by a proper environmental assessment, independent technical studies and transparent public consultation before any irreversible changes are made.

stories.title: Couple handed down life term for killing delivery boy near Lahore
summary: LAHORE: A sessions court on Thursday sentenced a man and his wife to life imprisonment for killing a delivery boy in Manga Mandi in 2023.

Additional District and Sessions Judge Shahzadi Najaf convicted Faran Qaiser and his wife, Amina, under Section 302(b) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) for intentional murder and sentenced them to life imprisonment.

The couple was also convicted under Section 201 of the PPC for causing evidence of the offence to disappear and each received a five-year rigorous imprisonment, along with a fine of Rs50,000, with a further simple imprisonment for a month on default.

stories.title: Welfarism is dead
summary: PARADED as amongst the greatest achievements of ‘advanced’ capitalist countries in the post-World War II period, the welfare state epitomised an era of widespread social prosperity.
Today, as mass protests rock France, the welfare state can officially be pronounced dead.

The welfare state itself was not a gift from above but a compulsion forced upon ruling classes of Western countries petrified of working-class populations at home and colonised people demanding self-rule in Asia and Africa.

stories.title: How to sustain research?
summary: Education research has not been a priority area for funding.
We urgently need a lot of high-quality research in education.

Recent investments, through DARE-RC in particular, have provided insights and lessons on how networks capable of producing the high-quality research needed to improve education outcomes can be created.

stories.title: Nuclear uncertainty
summary: In this regard, officials associated with Pakistan’s nuclear programme have rightly warned that India’s reported attempt to alter the strategic balance has heightened risks of escalation in South Asia.
India’s political class — as well as military officials — has issued jingoistic statements targeting Pakistan.
India should halt its highly provocative nuclear-armed submarine patrols and engage with Pakistan to ensure there are no misunderstandings, particularly in the strategic sphere.

stories.title: Balochistan Assembly defers move to abolish Sardari system
summary: Deputy Speaker Ghazala Gola, who presided over the sitting, announced that, in recognition of the late lawmaker’s services to the province, the assembly would adopt a condolence resolution and defer all other business until the next sitting.

Adopts resolution paying tribute to late education minister Maulana Hidayatur Rehman Baloch moved a motion seeking the postponement of the assembly’s proceedings until Monday, Oct 26, in recognition of the late former MPA’s services.

Presenting the condolence resolution, Mr Baloch said the house expressed deep grief and sorrow over the death of Sardar Nisar Ali Hazara, a former member of the Balochistan Assembly, who passed away on Oct 20.

stories.title: Labour federations oppose Pakistan Mineral Development Corporation's privatisation
summary: Speaking at a press conference and protest demonstration at the Quetta Press Club on Thursday, Mr Sultan urged the federal and provincial governments to withdraw the proposal and consult labour federations and workers’ representatives before taking any further action.
He vowed to continue the constitutional, legal and democratic struggle to protect workers’ rights.

stories.title: Three terrorists killed as forces foil attack in Gwadar
summary: GWADAR/QUETTA: Security forces killed three terrorists and foiled an attack on an unoccupied construction company camp in Gwadar, officials said on Thursday.
Security sources said forces had surrounded several other suspected terrorists near a hotel, and an operation was underway to thwart another attempted attack.
The law and order situation in the BP-250 area and its surroundings was under control following timely action by security forces and relevant intelligence agencies, the statement said.

stories.title: Fissures take a toll on PTI internal discipline
summary: Ms Yousafzai, however, had a heated exchange with PTI interim chief Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, which led to her quitting the WhatsApp groups.
A source told Dawn that Senator Yousafzai was among the party leaders who expressed a lack of trust in the PTI leadership over its failure to secure the release of Imran Khan.

PTI leader Sheikh Waqas Akram said Mr Naqvi had resigned, but Barrister Gohar rejected his resignation. “I hope that situation will be controlled as he [Firdous Shamim Naqvi] has not left any Whatsapp group of the party,” he added.

stories.title: National Assembly proceedings succumb to lack of quorum, again
summary: State Life Insurance Company After Question Hour, the National Assembly passed the Life Insurance (Nation­alisation) (Amend­ment) Bill, 2026.
The bill provides for the federal government to establish a company, to be known as State Life Insurance Company Limited, under the Companies Act, 2017 (XIX of 2017).
It states that the appointment of the company’s chief executive officer and board of directors will be made in accordance with the State-Owned Enterprises (SOE) Act and the Companies Act, 2017.

stories.title: Pakistan, EU flag security risks tied to Afghanistan
summary: The Afghanistan reference in the statement followed more explicit language in the joint communiqué issued after the eighth Pakistan-EU Stra­tegic Dialogue in Islamabad on June 1.

The reference is, moreover, significant because Pakistan has repeatedly urged international partners to press Afgha­nistan’s Taliban authorities to prevent terrorist groups from using Afghan territory to launch attacks across the border.

The language used in EU statements, while expressing concern on the terrorism threat from Afghanistan, indicates continuity with the latest dialogue reaffirming common ground between the two sides on the security risks associated with Afghanistan.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court bars arrest of KP Assembly deputy speaker
summary: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) has restrained the authorities from arresting Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Deputy Speaker Suriya Bibi until Nov 10, while allowing her to retain access to her official residence.

The court fixed Nov 10 for the next hearing of Ms Bibi’s petition against the sealing of her official residence and her anticipated arrest under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.

The lawyer also cited Section 27(2) of the act, which provided that the deputy speaker could not be arrested, detained or confined, and that her official residence could not be searched, entered or raided by a law enforcement agency during her term in office.

stories.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi sites claim four more lives
summary: Meanwhile, in a televised speech, the Houthi military spok­es­person, Yahya Saree, claimed attacks on Aramco facilities in the Red Sea city of Yanbu and on the defence ministry in Riyadh.

Hormuz attacks Meanwhile, the IRGC said on Thursday that four vessels involved in illegal oil transfers in the northern Persian Gulf were simultaneously hit and caught fire after being tracked by its forces on Wednesday.

Warning for pilgrims Separately, Pakistan’s Ministry of Religious Affairs has urged pilgrims to either use Iranian carriers or verify “every Iran-Iraq air sector before departure” when travelling between Iran and Iraq.

stories.title: Directorates of erstwhile Fata placed under ADS control
summary: Through a separate notification, the human resource management department temporarily transferred 30 posts in grades 17-20, along with their supporting ministerial and other staff, from the respective KP government departments to the ADS.
The notification said the officers posted to the ADS would also be allowed to retain and use the government vehicles already provided to them, along with associated facilities, until further orders.
On Wednesday, the ADS notified the names of five officials whose services the human resource management department had placed at its disposal as secretaries for the newly designated region.

stories.title: Woman dies, four others hurt in Shangla landslide
summary: After strenuous efforts, all five women were pulled from the debris and shifted to the Tehsil Headquarters Hospital in Puran for treatment.
In a separate incident, a tractor driver was killed when his vehicle plunged into a ravine in the Navy Kaly area of Puran tehsil on Thursday.
Police said the body was shifted to the Tehsil Headquarters Hospital in Puran, where doctors pronounced him dead.

stories.title: Over 45pc of 11th-grade students fail Pindi board annual exams
summary: RAWALPINDI: Nearly 45pc of students failed the 11th-grade intermediate annual examination 2026, conducted by the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) Rawalpindi.
The BISE Rawalpindi officially announced the results for the Intermediate Part I (11th-Grade).
According to the results, a total of 57,048 candidates registered for the examination, of whom 55,834 appeared.

stories.title: FIA busts illegal kidney transplant racket in capital; five held
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has busted an organised gang involved in illegal commercial kidney transplants, arresting five persons, seizing Rs1 million in cash besides freezing properties worth Rs87.5 million and impounding three vehicles.

According to a press release issued on Thursday, the FIA, along with Human Organ Transplantation Authority (HOTA), raided a premises in PWD Society, Islamabad, and found that recipient Mohammad Qasim had been transplanted a kidney of donor Ramzan Arshad in violation of law.
Investigations further revealed that the suspects had purchased properties in Islamabad from illicit proceeds of illegal transplants.

stories.title: UNIDO to mobilise $40m for Sindh rural development, climate-resilient projects
summary: Ms Haidara informed the chief minister that Pakistan had already signed the PCP framework with the UNIDO and that the organisation now intended to formulate a Sindh-specific programme based on the province’s development needs and priorities.

The meeting was informed that Community Resilient Settlement Development Plans (CRSDPs) had been prepared for around 300 villages across the five PAIDAR districts, laying the foundation for climate-informed planning and resilient infrastructure.

The programme is also supporting the development of Rural Growth Centres (RGCs) to improve access to public services, strengthen local economic activity, and create opportunities for enterprise development.

stories.title: Landslide leaves thousands stranded on Baltistan Road
summary: Local residents have expressed concern over the failure to implement safety measures on the road, which is frequently blocked by landslides and has witnessed numerous fatal accidents.
According to a statement issued by the Gilgit-Baltistan Disaster Management Authority (GBDMA), the road was completely blocked and traffic suspended.
Local residents have repeatedly complained about the failure to introduce adequate safety measures during the road’s reconstruction and alleged that the original project design was not implemented.

stories.title: Constituencies ‘re-described’ in KP sans mandatory public hearing
summary: NA-36 Hangu-cum-Orakzai-cum-Karak now comprises re-constituted Hangu district, Orakzai district, and two villages/mouzas — Darshi and Matho Khel — of Patwar Circle Mardan Khel, Qanungo Halqa Banda Daud Shah, Banda Daud Shah tehsil of Karak district.

NA-38 Karak now comprises Karak district re-co­nstituted vide April 2, 2024 notification, excluding the two villages of Darshi and Matho Khel of Banda Daud Shah tehsil, which have been shifted to NA-36.

NA-43 Tank-cum-Dera Ismail Khan-cum-Paha­rpur now comprises Tank district, Kulachi and Daraband tehsils plus Darazinda Sub-Division, excluding Koh-i-Bahara of Dera Ismail Khan district, and Paniala tehsil and part of Paharpur tehsil of newly created Paharpur district.

stories.title: 4 cops including DSP martyred, 2 terrorists killed during exchange of fire in KP's Karak: police
summary: LAKKI MARWAT: Four policemen, including two officials, were martyred and two terrorists were killed during an exchange of fire in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Karak district on Thursday, police said.

Police officers pay tribute to the martyred police personnel during funeral prayers in KP’s Karak on Oct 22. — photo courtesy KP police KP IGP Hameed paid tributes to the bravery, sense of duty, and professional commitment of the martyrs.

In September, two terrorists were killed in an intelligence-based operation in Lakki Marwat, and in August, a police constable was martyred and six officials were injured when an improvised explosive device was used to attack a police patrol van.

stories.title: Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye to meet European trio in Istanbul
summary: The R-4 group, which comprises Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye, emerged in March and has been focusing on regional security and mediation efforts between the United States and Iran.

A Turkish diplomatic source told Reuters that the seven countries would meet in the R-4+E-3 format for the first time at Turkiye’s initiative as wars involving Iran, Yemen and Ukraine threaten shipping routes and regional security.

Fidan will also tell counterparts that Turkiye has been working to stop the war in Ukraine from spreading to the Black Sea, pointing to the regional security risks posed by the conflict, the source said.

stories.title: Direct flights between Pakistan and Maldives on the horizon as PM stresses connectivity
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday announced that he had issued instructions for direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives.

The premier was addressing the Pakistan-Maldives Business Forum, attended by visiting Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, who arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday for a three-day trip at the invitation of PM Shehbaz.
The visit marks the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years, and comes as the two countries celebrate the 60th anniversary of their diplomatic relations, established in 1966.

stories.title: England's Brook hits record ODI double ton but Sri Lanka pull off epic chase in Rawalpindi clash
summary: England’s Harry Brook smashed the fastest double-century in One-Day International (ODI) history and became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format but Sri Lanka sealed a two-wicket win in their tri-series clash with one ball to spare in Rawalpindi on Thursday.
Brook’s scintillating performance ended with the final ball of England’s innings when he was caught by Sahan Arachchige off the bowling of Janith Liyanage.

The defeat leaves England bottom of the standings after losing both their matches, with Brook saying they need to win their next two games to reach the final in Lahore. “Unfortunately, it (the record) doesn’t matter now.

stories.title: PM vows to bring back progress to KP, assails PTI's 'callousness' during its tenures
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday vowed that the federal government, which now runs Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under governor’s rule, would make every effort possible to “bring back” progress to the province.

Emergency amid security challenges The Centre had imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

In the meeting, the governor — who is now in charge of running the province — assured Naqvi he would enforce all policies of the federal government and work together with the security forces for peace and prosperity of the province.

stories.title: NBC to take up GM corn cases on Friday
summary: The National Biosafety Committee (NBC) meets on Friday to consider a range of biosafety applications, including long-pending cases related to genetically modified (GM) corn technologies, according to a statement issued on Thursday.
CropLife Pakistan, an industry body representing seed and crop-protection companies, said approval of the pending GM corn biosafety licences would mark a milestone for agricultural biotechnology.

CropLife Pakistan Executive Director Rasheed Ahmed said such a move could accelerate the adoption of advanced seed technologies, which he said would improve farm productivity, food security and the competitiveness of the sector.

stories.title: PSX falls below 164,000 on oil fears
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange's (PSX) benchmark KSE-100 index fell below the 164,000-point level on Thursday, shedding over 2,000 points as escalating geopolitical tensions and rising international oil prices heightened investor concerns over the economic outlook.

Topline's market review noted that the KSE-100 index witnessed a sharp sell-off, shedding 2,007 points (-1.21%), as escalating geopolitical tensions and rising international oil prices weighed on investor sentiment.
Pakistan Refinery was the volume leader with trading in 25.88 million shares, losing Rs4.76 to close at Rs95.12.
